summary: This study investigated the role of pigment epithelium-derived factor receptor (PEDF-R) in the phagocytosis process of photoreceptor outer segment (POS) tips by RPE cells. Mice with conditional knockout of Pnpla2, a gene involved in POS degradation, accumulated lipid droplets and larger rhodopsin particles, and released less -hydroxybutyrate upon POS exposure. Inhibition of PEDF-R with a phospholipase A2 inhibitor or siRNA knockdown of PNPLA2 resulted in stalled rhodopsin degradation and reduced -hydroxybutyrate release, indicating a novel contribution of PEDF-R to POS degradation in the RPE.
